When you're applying for a credit card, you may wonder: "How good is the welcome offer I'm applying for?"

There's no simple answer to this question, but knowing the previous offers a card has had can help you determine what constitutes a good welcome offer. Getting any welcome offer is better than getting nothing at all, but you wouldn't want to apply for a card only to see a better offer a month later.

Generally, you’ll want good to excellent credit to qualify for many of the Capital One cards on this list, though other factors can also affect your approval odds.

We’ve collected and analyzed the offer history over the past few years for Capital One's most popular cards and determined the best time to apply for each.

Limited-time offer on the Capital One Venture Rewards Credit Card: Earn more than $1,000 in travel bonuses with a limited-time $300 Capital One Travel stays credit, plus earn 75,000 bonus miles once you spend $4,000 on purchases in the first three months from account opening.

It's important to note that we'll only discuss publicly available welcome offers. However, you might receive targeted offers that offer more bonus miles or cash back. You can also check for preapproved Capital One offers without affecting your credit score, which may help you find targeted offers that are higher than the publicly available bonus.

Keep in mind that offers may change at any time, and some of those mentioned below may not be available.

The bonus offer values throughout this guide are based on TPG’s November 2026 valuations and are not provided by the credit card issuer.

The Capital One Venture Rewards Credit Card earns an unlimited 2 miles per dollar spent on every purchase, plus 5 miles per dollar spent on hotels, rental cars and vacation rentals booked through Capital One Travel.

The card’s modest $95 annual fee, simple earning structure and solid return on everyday spending make it a keeper once you’re approved for it.

Here are the offers we've seen on the Capital One Venture Rewards:

Earn 75,000 bonus miles after spending $4,000 on purchases in the first three months of account opening (public offer).

The highest offer we've seen on this card allowed new cardholders to earn up to 100,000 bonus miles after spending $5,000 on purchases within the first three months of account opening.

When the bonus offers more than 75,000 miles — whether through additional miles or a travel credit — it meets our criteria for applying.

Learn more: Capital One Venture Rewards Credit Card

The Capital One Venture Business card is a straightforward option for business owners who want consistent travel rewards without having to track bonus categories. With a $95 annual fee, it offers simple earning rates, easy-to-use credits and flexible redemption options that help offset the cost year after year.

While it doesn’t come with premium perks like lounge access, its simplicity and solid earning structure make it a reliable long-term choice for everyday business spending.

The Venture Business's launch offer of up to 150,000 miles (75,000 miles after spending $7,500 on purchases in the first three months, plus an additional 75,000 miles after spending $30,000 on purchases in the first six months) is the best offer we've seen so far.

As a recently launched card, the Venture Business has only two bonus offers. Since there’s limited historical data, we recommend applying when the bonus is over 100,000 miles.

With plentiful, easy-to-understand perks, the Capital One Venture X is a no-brainer for all travelers, from luxury seekers to the more budget-minded, and the card practically pays for itself year after year.

Though the card carries a $395 annual fee, it offers a $300 annual credit toward bookings made through Capital One Travel and rewards cardholders with 10,000 bonus miles each account anniversary.

Here are the offers we've seen on the Capital One Venture X:

The highest offer we've seen on this card offered 100,000 bonus miles earned after spending $10,000 on purchases within the first six months of account opening.

When the bonus offer is 75,000 miles or higher, it's a good time to apply.

Learn more: Capital One Venture X Rewards Credit Card

The Venture X Business carries the same $395 annual fee as the personal version and offers the same major perks, including a $300 annual travel credit for bookings made through Capital One Business Travel and access to Capital One and participating Priority Pass lounges. It also carries the same earning rates as the Venture X.

Here are the offers we've seen on the Capital One Venture X Business:

The highest offer we've seen on this card is up to 400,000 bonus miles: Earn 200,000 miles after spending $30,000 on purchases in the first three months from account opening, plus an additional 200,000 miles after spending $150,000 on purchases in the first six months.

When the bonus offer is for more than 150,000 miles, it meets our criteria for applying.

Learn more: Capital One Venture X Business

While it comes with fewer perks, the Capital One VentureOne Rewards offers the same great redemption options as its sister cards, the Capital One Venture Rewards and the Capital One Venture X, with no annual fee. You’ll earn a flat 1.25 miles per dollar spent on everyday purchases.

Here are the offers we've seen on the Capital One VentureOne Rewards:

The highest offer we've seen allowed new cardholders to earn 40,000 bonus miles after spending $1,000 in the first three months of account opening.

When the bonus offers more than 20,000 miles — whether through additional miles or a travel credit — it meets our criteria for applying.

Learn more: Capital One VentureOne Rewards Credit Card

The biggest downsides to cash-back cards are low earning rates and a lack of bonus categories, but that’s definitely not true of the Capital One Savor Cash Rewards.

For no annual fee, the Savor offers strong cash-back earning rates on popular and often overlooked categories, including 3% back on dining, entertainment and popular streaming services.

Here are the offers we've seen on the Capital One Savor Cash Rewards:

The highest offer we've seen included a $100 Capital One Travel credit to use in the first year. Plus, new cardholders could receive a $200 cash bonus after spending $500 on purchases within the first three months of account opening.

When the bonus offer is $250 or more, it meets our criteria for applying.

Learn more: Capital One Savor Cash Rewards Credit Card

The Capital One Quicksilver Cash Rewards is another great card with no annual fee. It earns a reliable 1.5% cash back on all purchases, making it a perfect go-to card for the odd purchase that doesn’t fit in any bonus categories.

While many other cards offer higher earning potential in specific spending categories, this card offers the safety of knowing you’ll earn a solid 1.5% back no matter what you buy.

Here are the offers we've seen on the Capital One Quicksilver Cash Rewards:

The highest offer we've seen included a $100 Capital One Travel credit to use in the first year. Plus, new cardholders could receive a $200 cash bonus after spending $500 on purchases within the first three months of account opening.

When the bonus offer is $200 or higher, it meets our criteria for applying.

Learn more: Capital One Quicksilver Cash Rewards Credit Card

The Capital One Spark Cash Plus earns 2% cash back on all purchases and is ideal for business owners who want to earn reliable cash-back rewards on all their expenses. It is worth noting that this is a no-preset-spending-limit card, meaning cardholders must pay off their balances in full each month.

The card has a modest $150 annual fee that can be refunded after spending at least $150,000 in your card anniversary year.

Here are the offers we've seen on the Capital One Spark Cash Plus:

The highest welcome offer we've seen on this card offered up to $3,000: $500 after spending $5,000 on purchases in the first three months from account opening and $2,500 after spending $50,000 on purchases in the first six months from account opening.

When the bonus is $2,000 or higher, it meets our application criteria.

The Capital One Spark Cash earns 5% cash back on hotels and rental cars booked through Capital One Business Travel and 2% cash back on all other purchases. With the flat rate earning structure, the card is ideal for businesses with spending across different categories.

The card has a $0 introductory annual fee for the first year, then a $95 annual fee.

The Spark Cash is a traditional credit card that allows cardholders to carry a balance, offering more flexibility for businesses that don’t want to pay their balance in full each month.

Here are the offers we've seen on the Capital One Spark Cash:

The highest welcome offer we've seen on this card is $1,500 in cash back after spending $15,000 on purchases in the first three months from account opening.

When the bonus exceeds $1,000, it meets our application threshold.

The Capital One Spark Cash Select is a solid option for small-business owners who want to earn straightforward cash-back rewards without paying an annual fee.

The card earns unlimited 1.5% cash back on all purchases, plus 5% cash back on hotels and rental cars booked through Capital One Business Travel.

Here are the offers we've seen on the Capital One Spark Cash Select:

The highest welcome offer we've seen on this card is $750 cash back after spending $6,000 on purchases in the first three months from account opening.

When the bonus exceeds $500, it meets our application threshold.

Learn more: Capital One Spark Cash Select

Possibly, but Capital One restricts who is eligible to earn a welcome bonus, and the exact terms vary by card.

For several Capital One cards, you won't be eligible if you've received a new cardmember bonus on the same card — or, in some cases, another card in the same family — within the past 48 months. For example, the Venture Rewards terms exclude applicants who have received a new cardmember bonus on the Venture Rewards or Venture X within the past 48 months.

Because these restrictions vary among cards and can change, check the specific card's current offer terms before applying.

Capital One welcome offers can fluctuate, so it can sometimes make sense to hold off on applying. While there’s no guarantee that a better offer will come along, looking at a card’s offer history can help you decide whether to apply now or wait.

#6077. Frontier Airlines Passenger Refuses To Leave, Demands Flight Attendant Apologize To Her 4-Year Old Over Toilet Dispute

A Frontier Airlines passenger says she refused to get off her San Francisco–Denver flight until a flight attendant apologized to her four year old son. The argument began with a request to flush the toilet after the frightened boy had left the lavatory. The mother says things escalated when she overheard the crew member making fun of his fear. I don’t think asking for a little help with a frightened child is outrageous. If the flight attendant mocked him, an apology was appropriate. But the mother wasn’t entitled to make getting off the aircraft conditional on receiving one. She says her son was afraid of loud toilet flushes and needed the bathroom about 40 minutes before landing. She tried offering headphones and offering to flush for him. Eventually she reassured him that they could ask a flight attendant to help. She says she asked the flight attendant near the lavatory to flush after they’d washed their hands and left. The response was, He can flush it. It’s not that loud. The flight attendant added that this was a new plane. The mother says she dropped the request, but while she and her son were inside the lavatory, she heard the crew member talking to a colleague: Can you believe that mom? Scared of a toilet? Come on. She says her son heard it too and asked whether they were talking about him. The mother flushed the toilet herself, with her son waiting outside and the door closed. At deplaning she confronted the flight attendant and demanded an apology to the boy. She says the crewmember responded “Have a good day,” so she announced: I’m not getting off this airplane until you apologize to my son for literally making fun of him for being afraid of something. A pilot emerged from the cockpit, the flight attendant apologized, and she left. She also says a couple of passengers applauded and another mother praised her. She’s since posted a clarification: she says she also asked the flight attendant to stand with her son while she flushed. She also says her analytics show viewers watched an average of 23% of the original video and that’s why so many people seem to have missed that she did, in fact, flush the toilet herself. She wanted help pressing a button once they were away, or standing beside the child briefly. A polite refusal would be reasonable. In terms of what the flight attendant’s actual duty is, the union contract‘s article 23.I assigns general tidying and replenishing lavatory supplies, but says, “Flight Attendants will not clean the aircraft.” Pushing the button isn’t cleaning, but they don’t have broad lavatory duties. The claim that it’s a new airplane doesn’t mean the toilet isn’t loud. Aircraft vacuum toilets can be startling. Brigham Young University researchers spent two years developing a quieter aircraft toilet, citing parents’ concerns about children being afraid to use them. A quieter cabin can even make the flush stand out more. I’ve written about flight attendants mocking passengers for using the bathroom during boarding. The mother makes herself much harder to sympathize with in her video, though. She calls the employee an “old bitch” and tells her to “know your f’ing role.” I sided with the expectation that parents clean up after their children when Anthony Bass complained about his pregnant wife being asked to pick up their child’s popcorn on United. Parents should take responsibility. And her refusal to leave is absurd. Complain to the airline, don’t inconvenience other passengers trying to get off the plane. #6076. Zinke PAC gave to family foundation he was investigated for

Rep. Ryan Zinke, R-Mont., leaves a meeting of the House Republican Conference at the Capitol Hill Club on July 15, 2025. (Tom Williams/CQ Roll Call)

Outgoing Montana GOP Rep. Ryan Zinke gave $200,000 in campaign cash to a family foundation headed by his wife that was once at the center of a federal investigation and an ethics scandal that led him to resign as Interior secretary in 2019.

The gift, which has not previously been reported, was made on Aug. 31 from Zinke’s leadership political action committee to the nonprofit Great Northern Veterans Peace Foundation, campaign finance records show. The donation is more than the foundation has reported receiving in any year since it was founded nearly two decades ago.

Zinke’s wife, son, and sister currently serve on its board of directors, according to the foundation’s annual filing with the state of Montana.

In a brief interview, Zinke denied that any portion of the money transferred to the foundation will directly benefit him or any of his family members who sit on the board of directors. “No, no, never," he said when asked if any family members will draw a salary from the gift.

The money will instead go to building a storage barn and kid’s sledding park on the property controlled by the foundation, Zinke said.

None of the records indicate Zinke violated the law or directly benefited from the gift to his foundation.

“While it's not uncommon for a politician to transfer leftover money from a political war chest to charity, it is pretty rare for a politician to transfer leftover political funds to a charity that they or a relative controls,” said Michael Beckel, director of money in politics reform at Issue One, a bipartisan group that seeks to reduce influence of money in politics.

Instead, outgoing members typically transfer remaining campaign cash to local party committees or candidates, Beckel added.

Ethics experts say Zinke’s move highlights ongoing concerns over the broad latitude campaign finance law gives leadership PACs in how they spend money.

“I definitely think it is something to be concerned about,” said Stuart McPhail, director of campaign finance litigation at Citizens for Responsibility and Ethics in Washington, a nonprofit watchdog.

“Leadership PACs are really nothing more than personal slush funds under today's rules,” he said, noting that unlike regular campaign committees, member leadership PACs are not prohibited from donating to charities or organizations that could directly benefit the member or relative.

Zinke, a former Navy SEAL who commanded special forces during the Iraq War, converted his traditional campaign committee to a leadership PAC — Commander Zinke Leadership Fund — in March 2026, shortly after announcing he would not run for reelection. It last reported having $1.4 million cash on hand in October of this year.

It marks the second time one of Zinke’s political committees made a payment to the organization. In 2019, the committee Zinke ran during his earlier years in Congress — he served one term in the House before being tapped as Trump’s first-term Interior secretary — gave over $11,000 to the foundation before winding down operations.

The Great Northern Veterans Peace Foundation was founded by Zinke and his wife in 2007 in his hometown of Whitefish, Mont., with plans to provide winter recreational activities for children. Its latest tax filing reports revenue of $15,000 and roughly equal expenses in 2024 for snow plowing and park maintenance.

Zinke’s dealings with the organization were the subject of an ongoing inspector general investigation when he resigned as Interior secretary in January 2019.

Investigators ultimately did not find that Zinke violated conflict-of-interest laws, but they concluded that he failed to comply with federal ethics obligations and “misused his official position in violation of federal regulations.” The Justice Department declined to prosecute Zinke.

Zinke stepped down from the foundation in 2017, shortly after his Senate confirmation. But investigators found that he continued to represent the organization in negotiations with the developers of a commercial project adjacent to the foundation’s land and lied to an ethics agent about his involvement in the project.

The project’s investors included David Lesar, then-chairman of oil services company Halliburton.

Another Zinke-tied leadership PAC has previously raised eyebrows in Washington.

Supporting Electing American Leaders PAC — known as SEAL PAC — where Zinke serves as chairman, has been marred by accusations that it funneled money to political consultants instead of candidates. A 2022 CQ Roll Call analysis found that 87 percent of the PAC’s spending went to operating expenses.

The PAC also made recurring monthly payments to a company registered to Zinke’s son, Wolfgang Zinke, and based at a Zinke family-owned home in Whitefish.

SEAL PAC’s executive director, Rob Catron, maintained that the payments constitute a consulting fee to Wolfgang Zinke for management of the PAC website, among other tasks. “He earns every penny of it,” Catron said.

Since May 2022, the PAC has given roughly $270,000 to Wolfgang Zinke’s company, FG Solutions, for mailing and printing, records show — more than any individual candidate or committee supported by the PAC. The company also received $5,000 from a related super PAC, SEAL PAC USA, which can solicit unlimited contributions for independent expenditures but can’t donate directly to candidates.

Montana corporate records show Wolfgang Zinke founded FG Solutions – which says it provides services including “personal assistant and any lawful purpose” – just 10 days before it received its first payment from the PAC in 2022.

Catron defended how the PAC spends money on veterans running for the House, arguing that it takes money to raise money.

“We raise a lion’s share of our funding through national direct mail fundraising, which is very expensive to do,” he said, citing the PAC’s use of a national text message fundraising campaign as a major expense.

SEAL PAC raised about $9.6 million this election cycle, distributing about $1.1 million to GOP lawmakers and candidates, according to Federal Election Commission filings. Most of the committee's funds went to operating expenses, including over $3 million paid to Direct Support Services, a Washington-based vendor, for direct mail postage.

Zinke’s not the only lawmaker to face scrutiny over how they spent surplus campaign cash in recent years.

In 2023, Sen. Bernie Sanders, I-Vt., set off alarm bells for transferring $200,000 from his campaign committee to The Sanders Institute, a nonprofit founded by his wife and stepson, following a $350,000 donation from his 2020 presidential campaign coffers.

The organization briefly shut down during Sanders’ presidential run in 2019 to avoid the appearance of impropriety.

Sanders’ stepson, David Driscoll — a former executive at Nike and snowboard manufacturer Burton — is listed on the think tank’s website as its executive director, drawing a six-figure annual salary according to tax filings.

It’s unusual, though not unheard of, for campaign committees to pay family members of the candidate for bona fide work.

“If [Wolfgang Zinke] is actually performing this work, he’s qualified to do it, and this is his typical market rate for this kind of contract, then it would be permissible, even if this was a campaign account,” McPhail said about SEAL PAC's payments.

But the payments could present a legal “gray area” over whether personal-use restrictions apply to certain PACs, according to McPhail.

#6074. Delta Pilot Reportedly Fired For Answering His Phone While Taxiing—Similar Stories Go Back At Least 5 Years

A Delta Air Lines first officer allegedly answered his cellphone while taxiing out in Atlanta on his first trip at the airline. The captain returned to the gate, had him removed, and the new hire lost his job, according to an account shared by the Black Box Aviation Podcast and covered by Live and Let’s Fly. The first officer was reportedly flying trips under a check pilot’s supervision as part of their initial operating experience. The Black Box Aviation Podcast’s account, November 17, 2026 There’s no identified pilot, flight number, aircraft type or date for the alleged incident. The podcast’s companion article repeats the allegation but doesn’t fill in those details. A Similar Delta Story Was Being Told In 2021 In a July 3, 2021 discussion on Airline Pilot Central, a moderator responded to a comment about how hard it was to get fired at Delta: Like answering your cell phone during taxi. On OE. In a follow-up, he said he’d heard the story from a line check pilot. That version included the employee defending his need to stay connected during a subsequent meeting with management. By July 2025, another forum version had the Delta pilot answering because FedEx was calling about a job. Other posters mocked how often this same kind of story gets told about different airlines. And in an older Reddit discussion of pilot firings, one commenter said they’d heard a first officer using Tinder while taxiing during training story at all four airlines where they’d worked. The comments at Live and Let’s Fly reflect a split between calling it longstanding airline folklore versus supporting strict enforcement of the phone prohibition. I had much the same reaction to September’s claim that 120 pilots had been grounded for using inflight Wi-Fi. There’s a real rule against personal device use, but the particular claims weren’t well-supported. The First Officer Has Work To Do During Taxi Even when the captain has control of he aircraft, the first officer needs to monitor the aircraft’s position, clearances and other traffic. Taxiing through Atlanta isn’t downtime before the flight starts. The sterile cockpit rule covers taxi. Federal regulations prohibit distracting, nonessential activities during critical phases of flight. Those include taxi, takeoff and landing, as well as other operations below 10,000 feet except cruise. Personal phone use isn’t permissible at cruise Wireless devices and laptops are restricted at a flight crewmember’s duty station throughout flight time. (Approved electronic charts and manuals are different. It’s the device’s use, rather than who owns it, that controls. ) I’ve written that pilots should be allowed to be human, rather than expected to behave like robots throughout a long flight. That doesn’t mean taking a personal call while moving a passenger jet through an airport. Phone Distraction Has Caused Real Problems I covered a Jetstar phone-distraction incident involving a Darwin–Singapore flight where the crew hadn’t lowered the landing gear when a warning sounded at 720 feet. Their go-around began at 392 feet. The Australian investigation found that incoming message alerts sounded, the first officer saw the captain occupied with his phone, and the captain said he was unlocking it and turning it off. Jetstar added a reminder to switch phones off to its takeoff checklist and moved its landing checklist completion requirement from 500 feet to 1,000 feet, and incorporated the incident into pilot training. #6072. Now hiring: Staff to power Democrats’ probes

Ranking member Jamie Raskin, D-Md., arrives at the Rayburn Building for a House Judiciary Committee hearing in February. He will be a key player in leading oversight efforts next year — and so will Democratic staff. (Tom Williams/CQ Roll Call)

Democrats in Congress have promised to hit the ground running with sprawling oversight investigations in the new year, making the most of their coming majority.

That means staffing up major committees. And for the dozens of attorneys and other aides preparing to take on a belligerent Trump administration that has cast Democratic oversight as potentially criminal, the job will come with extra scrutiny.

Arya Hariharan, former chief oversight counsel to Sen. Richard J. Durbin on the Senate Judiciary Committee and now a partner at Holland & Knight, said the pressure will be on from day one.

“Are you prepared to not sleep very much and know that every single thing you do is going to be scrutinized, every footnote, every comma?” Hariharan said.

Still, the way Hariharan sees it, serving on the Hill is worth it. “I hope they all fall in love with it because it’s a lovely place to work,” she says of staffers headed there for the first time.

The work done by attorneys and other staff in oversight probes can quickly become part of constitutional law. When Trump adviser Peter Navarro defied a subpoena from Democrats investigating the Jan. 6, 2021, attack on the Capitol, it touched off debates about executive privilege and contempt of Congress. Probes of Hunter Biden led to similar court fights.

Some questions have gone all the way up to the Supreme Court, like in Trump v. Mazars, when the House fought to access Trump’s business records during his first administration in furtherance of toughening up government ethics laws.

There’s every indication that pressure will continue in the new Congress. James Melendres, a partner at Snell & Wilmer, said Democrats are poised for aggressive oversight efforts, even if they know it could be tough to make headway against litigation resistant administration officials.

“Democrats are going to have less than two years to show results. I think they are going to move really fast,” Melendres said.

Democrats will likely soon start to send out preservation letters to private companies, institutions and others they intend to probe in the new year, if they haven’t already, Melendres said.

“There may be significant pushback from the administration, from agencies and individual government officials who receive requests. I think third-party, nongovernment agencies and individuals are going to be high on the list for these committees,” he said.

In addition to the hiring that happens over the next few weeks, House Democrats will have major decisions to make about chamber and committee rules for the new Congress, including who will hold subpoena authority. And off-Hill observers will be watching closely.

“For companies, for individuals and their counsel, mapping all of that is going to be a big part of the job between now and early January,” Melendres said.

Lawmakers need to nail down funding levels for congressional committees and staff — the amount of money involved can make a big difference in how big investigations get. Major committees, and major investigations, take a large amount of staff and expertise to get going.

For instance, the special House panel that investigated the Jan. 6 attack on the Capitol spent about $14 million in less than 18 months, including for dozens of staffers.

Standing committees, such as Oversight and Judiciary, take a good chunk of change, too. In 2025 the House spent $12.9 million on the House Oversight and Government Reform panel, and $13.1 million on the House Judiciary Committee.

Those expenditures mean dozens of staff working long hours to review documents, send letters, send subpoenas and conduct interviews. Judiciary ranking member Jamie Raskin, D-Md., who is expected to serve as chair next year, said he wouldn’t get into specifics yet about how many resources the new Congress may devote to oversight efforts.

“But we are talking about the most corrupt administration in the history of the United States, and this is an overwhelming and daunting task that faces us,” Raskin said.

The Trump administration itself has already signaled it intends to push back forcefully on congressional oversight efforts.

Earlier this month, President Donald Trump described Democrats’ vows to investigate his administration as “extortion at the highest level” and called for the Justice Department to “look into this criminal act, immediately!”

Days later, the White House counsel sent a letter saying that subpoena threats from House Oversight ranking member Robert Garcia, D-Calif., and others “may cross the line into blatant criminality.”

U.S. Attorney Aaron Reitz for the Southern District of Texas followed up with letters of his own to Sens. Richard Blumenthal, D-Conn.; Elizabeth Warren, D-Mass.; and Elissa Slotkin, D-Mich., urging them to preserve documents tied to their promised oversight.

“The American people are entitled to freely associate without their elected officials terrorizing them with aggressive, harassing government action,” Reitz’s letter to Warren said.

Members of the incoming majority have signaled they intend to defend themselves and their probes, and Blumenthal said he won’t be deterred by the letter.

“There’s no way that I’m going to be intimidated or bullied. It would be laughable and ludicrous, but it is a clear abuse and misuse of prosecutorial powers and weaponization by the Department of Justice,” said Blumenthal, who serves as the top Democrat on the Senate Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Permanent Subcommittee on Investigations.

As for Raskin, he called the White House counsel letter and other missives “absurd on its face.”

“I’m sure they would love to get into a whole series of letters and counter-letters and litigation. They’re trying to distract everybody from the fact that they just lost the worst landslide electoral repudiation in at least a half century in America, and so they’re going to pick a fight,” Raskin told reporters.

Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, D-N.Y., the likely incoming speaker, told reporters last week that he intended oversight efforts in his chamber to be led by Raskin and Garcia.

“We haven’t ruled anything in. We haven’t ruled anything out. We’re going to follow the facts. We’re going to apply the law. We’re going to be guided by the Constitution, and we’re going to let the chips fall where they may,” Jeffries said.

Democrats have already publicly listed a handful of job postings for oversight staff and counsel, ranging from the Science to Armed Services to Judiciary panels, set to start early next year.

Beyond those hires, House Democrats will have to make one major pick they haven’t yet announced — the House counsel. The position, first created in the 1970s, is hired by the majority and advocates for the chamber in court. That attorney, along with a group of bipartisan House leaders controlled by the majority, will steer the chamber’s legal strategy.

In prior Democratic Congresses, that office has been active in court; Doug Letter frequently argued on behalf of the Democratic House majority seeking to enforce subpoenas on behalf of congressional committees. The position is held by Matthew Berry in the current Republican-controlled House.

“I mean, I think a lot of people are interested in that job,” Raskin said.

Believe it or not, Thanksgiving is around the corner. Families around the country are working on their grocery lists — and maybe keeping an eye on the wild shopping days that come after we dine with family and friends. If you're hoping to snag some great travel deals for Black Friday, Cyber Monday and Travel Tuesday, TPG has a dedicated page where you can find our favorite deals.

And if you need a little inspiration for your next vacation, we just released our annual Where to Go list for 2027. This year's list ranges from Texas Hill Country to Tunisia and from the Cayman Islands to Kazakhstan.

Now, here's the hotel news you need to know about from this week.

Hyatt is expanding its lifestyle footprint with the opening of the first Andaz in Australia. The Andaz Gold Coast, located in sunny Queensland, will have 202 rooms and plans to "redefine coastal luxury through a distinctive blend of expressive Australian design and immersive experiences inspired by the people, places, and creative spirit of the Gold Coast," according to a statement from Hyatt. The property is near the beaches of Broadbeach, and features a series of bars and restaurants, plus a lively pool club offering live music and community-focused barbecues.

Also in Queensland, Brisbane will welcome a Park Hyatt in 2031, ahead of the 2032 Brisbane Olympics. Brisbane is one of my favorite cities, so I can't wait (though I'll have to) for the 201-room property not far from Suncorp Stadium, which will host a series of soccer and rugby events. Many details about the property are still under wraps, but if it's even half as great as the Park Hyatt Sydney, we know it'll be a great hotel.

If you haven't had the chance to visit Houston, I can't recommend it enough. The city is home to diverse cultures, incredible food and the Houston Livestock Show and Rodeo, one of the biggest rodeos in the world. If you find yourself in Beyoncé's hometown, consider a stay at the JW Marriott Houston Downtown, which just completed a years-long head-to-toe remodel. The hotel now features fresh rooms, including 56 new rooms, a redesigned lobby restaurant and a total revamp of the hotel's food and beverage offerings.

Monti, my favorite neighborhood in Rome, feels like stepping back in time. Or, at least into a movie set, thanks to its beautiful vine-covered walls, cobblestone streets and lively energy near the Colosseum. In 2028, it'll also be home to Hortus Monti Rome, part of Hilton's upscale LXR Hotels & Resorts. The hotel is spread across six historic Umbertine-era buildings, according to a statement from Hilton and features a central garden, a spa, bars and restaurants and more.

Until then, Hilton fans should check into Rome Cavalieri, one of the most popular Waldorf Astoria hotels in the world.

The Coke versus Pepsi debate is a serious one, and people tend to have strong opinions about which is better. While I'm a Diet Dr. Pepper fanatic myself, it looks like Hyatt is doubling down on its relationship with Pepsi. The company just renewed its contract, making PepsiCo the preferred beverage partner across 700 Hyatt properties in the United States. The agreement also extends to certain PepsiCo snack products.

Earlier this year, Marriott ousted Pepsi and made Coca-Cola its "global beverage partner across several categories, including carbonated soft drinks and a growing range of hydration and functional beverages."

#6070. Hermès Carry-On Costs $10,450 Used—Travelers Are Worried About Gate Checking It, And That’s The Problem

A Hermès carry on bag with two horse heads on the front is listed for $10,450 used, and travelers on Reddit are imagining the argument with a gate agent who wants to check it. I like good luggage. I’ve been using my Rimowa Salsa Deluxe for about a decade. But I don’t understand spending $10,000 on a carry on if it means worrying more about what happens to the bag than to everything inside it. Here’s the Hermès Toile & Clemence R.M.S. Cabine 55. The asking price was $11,000, reduced 5%. Hermès currently lists its Quadrige horse print cabin suitcase for $13,400 new. Imagine the fight with the Gate Agent over checking this! What You’re Getting For The Money Reactions in the Delta thread range from hating the design to insisting that anyone with $10,000 luggage must fly private, which doesn’t make sense. They probably have no money left for even Comfort+. And there are happy owners. In a discussion among Hermès enthusiasts, one owner praises the construction and smooth wheels, while acknowledging they fly private most of the time (heh). Others worry about weight, wear and having to check it. PurseBop’s detailed owner review loves how it rolls and the ability to customize details. But the review also finds less packing space than in a Louis Vuitton Horizon because of where the telescopic handle sits. That handle arrangement also makes balancing a large tote on top less convenient. People should buy what they want. Part of being human is valuing aesthetics. A beautiful object can make someone happy every time they use it, and that has value. This particular design doesn’t do much for me, but other people don’t need to share my taste. Why I’ll Pay More For Good Luggage I used to buy whatever inexpensive bag I could find. As I traveled more, I became willing to pay for something that rolled easily, balanced properly, held what I needed and fit comfortably in the overhead bin. I wrote about that tradeoff back in 2015. A few hundred dollars spread across years of frequent travel can be a small cost per trip. Better wheels are nice every time you walk through an airport. A handle or zipper that doesn’t break saves you a hassle at exactly the moment you don’t have time for one. I still like my decade-old Rimowa Salsa Deluxe. I find Tumi overpriced for what it is, prefer Briggs & Riley for quality, and think Delsey Helium is decent at the value end. My experience with Rimowa customer service has been atrocious. When part of my handle broke, I got disconnected calls, unanswered emails and a runaround between their repair teams. By the time I reached the right people, they told me my warranty had expired in the year and a half during Covid since I’d first contacted them. First Class Doesn’t Guarantee Your Bag Stays With You Some Reddit commenters figure the owner would board early or fly first class, so gate checking wouldn’t be an issue. It doesn’t change the size of the bins on a small aircraft or help when a late connection puts you among the last passengers to board. Hermès lists its current Quadrige cabin suitcase at 22.4 inches tall. A fairly standard published limit is 22 inches, including wheels and handles. I hate gate checking bags. I don’t want my belongings lost or delayed, and I don’t want to waste time at baggage claim. When a bag comes back at the aircraft door, there’s still the wait and the extra handling. I’ve made this argument before about Louis Vuitton luggage. A bag’s job is to make its contents easy to transport and protect them along the way. If the bag itself becomes something you have to protect from ordinary travel, you’re missing the point. In 2023 I covered a traveler upset about scuffs on a Louis Vuitton carry on after Delta required it to be checked. That same year, a woman made her boyfriend give up his shirt to wrap around her $200 suitcase. This particular bag is apparently in “Excellent” condition, with “minor scratches at hardware.” For $10,450, at least somebody else has already taken care of the breaking it in. Topics on this pageCarry on BagGate checkingHermèsLuggageBriggs & RileyDelta Air LinesLouis VuittonRedditRimowa GmbHTumi Inc.+6 more More From View from the Wing

OMG – Fly private – if you can affort $10K on a bag – then fly private! I have yet to have Delta First class give me crap though for a 22.5 inch bag!

And if they lose that suitcase, you’ll get a maximum of $1200 compensation.

You don’t get a pass on gate checking just because you spent too much on your bag

When the bag is worth more than the drugs you’re smuggling in it, there’s an issue.

It’s like luxury cars – if you worry about getting it dinged, you bought one you couldn’t afford. (For luggage, I like the German brand Titan. Tough but light polycarbonate 4-spinners. Long-lasting, but no luggage lasts forever if it’s being used.)

The nice luggage is for the car. The collectible stuff is in dust covers in the house ( insured ). The Tumi you cannot destroy

I only buy used Tumi luggage for a fraction of the price new. Most has hardly been used.

A bag’s job is to make its contents easy to transport and protect them along the way. If the bag itself becomes something you have to protect from ordinary travel, you’re missing the point.

My logic is to buy relatively inexpensive luggage, treat it as a consumable, and get on with my travels.

@Denver Refugee — “Mmm… ‘consumable’ baggage… ahrrrr” — Homer Simpson.

I have shifted a bunch of my trips to using a free collapsible Nike duffel bag which weighs less than 2lbs empty and which I got free from some professional sports event. So my wheeled cabin-bags from Rimowa, Tumi, Samsonite, etc are getting less use because I have increasingly substituted to the duffel bag.

#6068. Latino Democrats celebrate midterm gains, with warning for party

California Rep. Linda T. Sánchez, here at a 2020 news conference in the Capitol Visitor Center, is the chair of BOLD PAC. (Tom Williams/CQ Roll Call)

Latino voters moved sharply away from Republicans this year, and a record number of Latino Democratic candidates were elected.

But California Rep. Linda T. Sánchez has a warning for her fellow Democrats.

“Latino voters gave Democrats a two-year lease, but it expires in 2028 unless the party changes its playbook for good,” said Sánchez, who leads the campaign arm of the Congressional Hispanic Caucus.

Failure to address rising costs and push back against President Donald Trump’s immigration agenda could once again scramble the political calculus and spark another realignment in two years, said House Democratic Caucus Chair Pete Aguilar of California.

“While Latinos shifted towards Democrats and … gave us this mandate as a party, Democrats must continue to earn their trust, not just every two years, but every single day,’’ he said.

Leaders of the Congressional Hispanic Caucus joined newly elected Latino members on Tuesday for a news conference to celebrate the recent wins and the role the group played in securing the House majority for Democrats. The caucus will boast 55 members in the next Congress, its largest roster ever, according to Sánchez.

BOLD PAC, the caucus’ campaign arm, invested heavily in Latino candidates this year, including in primaries.

California Rep. Salud Carbajal noted that BOLD PAC raised more than $18.5 million this cycle, which helped candidates leverage outside money.

Working-class majority-Latino districts in South Texas, Arizona and California were among the areas that provided Democrats with their biggest wins. Democrats capitalized on voter dissatisfaction over rising costs, the very issue that helped Trump and the GOP make significant gains among Hispanic voters just two years earlier.

But the wins weren’t limited to districts with sizable Latino populations.

Rep.-elect Denise Powell, who flipped a swing seat in Nebraska, credited BOLD PAC for playing a key role in her win.

“Yes, there are Latinos in Omaha, and those Latinos actually helped decide this race,’’ she said. “BOLD believed in me as a candidate, but they also believed in our community.”

Rep.-elect Bobby Pulido, who came to politics after a successful career as a Latin Grammy-winning Tejano singer, flipped a redrawn South Texas border district that Trump would have carried by 18 points in 2024.

“A lot of people feel like they don't belong to either party. But there's one thing about Latinos is we belong to each other,’’ Pulido said. “It's very hard to be a Latino right now in this country. … I expect to see us united, more united than ever, because it's a tough time right now.”

Several of the winning candidates deployed novel strategies to reach voters. Pulido famously began performing at quinceañeras after his Republican opponent dismissed him as a performer.

Colorado Rep.-elect Manny Rutinel, who flipped a battleground district north of Denver, attended World Cup and Broncos watch parties. “If people don't hear our message, then it doesn't matter,’’ he said.

The candidates “met those voters where they were,’’ Sánchez said. “They went into those communities and interacted in a very real and meaningful way. That's something I think that strategists or consultants don't always get. It's not just about pumping out lots of television commercials.”

Amid those successes for Latino Democrats, Florida, home to one of the largest Latino electorates in the country, was a different story. Republicans held all three majority-Latino districts in the Sunshine State, though former news anchor Eliott Rodriguez, the son of Cuban immigrants, came within half a percentage point of unseating GOP Rep. María Elvira Salazar in a district that backed Trump by 15 points in 2024.

BOLD PAC did have a victory to celebrate in Florida, with Rep. Darren Soto, the deputy chair of the Congressional Hispanic Caucus, narrowly prevailing in a district that Republicans redrew as one that no longer had a Latino majority.

“The redistricting wars ended up failing because of the investment by BOLD PAC,’’ Soto said.

#6067. Citi AAdvantage Globe Card Review—I Applied For The Bonus, But The Flight Streak Perk Is Why I Like It

I receive compensation for content and many links on this blog. Be aware that websites may earn compensation when a customer clicks on a link, when an application is approved, or when an account is opened. Citibank is an advertising partner of this site, as is American Express, Chase, Capital One, and others. Any opinions expressed in this post are my own, and have not been reviewed, approved, or endorsed by my advertising partners. I do not write about all offers that are available -- instead focusing on miles, points, and cash back (and currencies that can be converted into the same). Terms apply to the offers and benefits listed on this page.

I applied for the Citi® / AAdvantage® Globe™ Mastercard® [See rates and fees] when it launched because it was a new card I wanted to try up close and because it carried an initial bonus I hadn’t had yet. I wound up with two Globe cards, though: the one I applied for, and a second when my Barclays AAdvantage Aviator Silver card became a Globe.

The reason I like having a Globe beyond the initial bonus is its Flight Streak benefit. You can earn up to 15,000 additional Loyalty Points each year for American Airlines flights, without putting spending on the card. I already have the Citi® / AAdvantage BusinessTM World Elite Mastercard® [See rates and fees] and Citi® / AAdvantage® Executive World Legend Mastercard® [See rates and fees] cards for different reasons. Business is the best one for spending towards status, while Executive gives me lounge access and more bonus Loyalty Points. But Globe adds something neither of those provides.

At $350 a year, Citi AAdvantage Globe Card is worth considering both as your main American Airlines benefits card and as an addition to the cards you already have. But you need to value the benefits and having two Globes doesn’t double the Flight Streak bonus.

The Citi AAdvantage Globe Card awards 5,000 Loyalty Points for every four qualifying American Airlines flight segments, up to three times per status qualification year. Qualifying Segments Flown Total Flight Streak Loyalty Points 4 5,000 8 10,000 12 15,000 These are segments, so a roundtrip with a connection each way is four flights. Three of those trips can generate the full bonus. Six nonstop roundtrips would do it, too. You don’t have to buy the tickets with your Globe card. You can use another card for its rewards or protections, or fly on a ticket your employer purchases, and still earn the bonus on your qualifying travel. The qualification year runs March 1 through the last day of February. Flights must be taken after you become a primary Globe cardmember. Qualifying flights are marketed or operated by American Airlines or American Eagle and ordinarily must earn AAdvantage miles. The terms expressly include American’s basic economy segments. Award flights don’t count. The benefit belongs to the primary cardmember. Adding authorized users doesn’t give each person their own Flight Streak bonus. Citi allows 8–10 weeks after qualifying flight segments post for the additional Loyalty Points to appear. (In practice it happens quickly.) These are points toward status, not another 15,000 miles you can spend on awards. For someone already flying American regularly, this can reduce how much additional spending or other earning they need to do to reach their next status level. There’s no requirement to divert $20,000 or $50,000 of purchases from a more rewarding card. I view the card as an inexpensive way to purchase Loyalty Points which are valuable both for earning status and for additional milestone rewards. Globe And Executive Work Together—Two Globes Don’t Double The Bonus When I analyzed Globe at launch, my criticism was that Citi wasn’t giving customers much reason to keep spending on it. From the customer’s perspective, though, that’s potentially a good thing. I earn the flight bonus while putting spend wherever it makes the most sense. The Executive card by contrast includes 10,000 bonus Loyalty Points at each of 50,000, 90,000, 165,000 and 240,000 Loyalty Points earned in a qualification year. Globe’s Flight Streak bonus can stack with that. Someone meeting all the requirements can earn up to 55,000 bonus Loyalty Points from the two products combined. The final Executive bonus requires reaching 240,000 Loyalty Points, so that maximum isn’t a shortcut to earning Executive Platinum from scratch. My second Citi AAdvantage Globe Card came from the April 2026 Barclays conversion. I initially wondered whether two accounts would generate two sets of flight bonuses. American subsequently confirmed to me that they wouldn’t. The Initial Bonus And Annual Fee The current offer for the Citi AAdvantage Globe Card is 60,000 AAdvantage miles after $4,000 in purchases within the first three months. The annual fee is $350, isn’t waived the first year, and there’s no additional charge for authorized users. There are no foreign transaction fees. The bonus restriction is specific to the Citi AAdvantage Globe Card: you can’t have received a new account bonus on Globe within the past 48 months, and there’s also a restriction involving another Citi account with a recent bonus that you converted into Globe. Simply having the Executive or Business card doesn’t disqualify you. What You Earn When You Spend The card’s earning categories are: Eligible Purchases AAdvantage Miles Per Dollar Loyalty Points Per Dollar AAdvantage Hotels bookings 6 1 American Airlines purchases 3 1 Restaurants, including takeout and delivery 2 1 Eligible transit, including taxis, rideshares and public transit 2 1 Other purchases 1 1 Bonus categories increase redeemable miles, not Loyalty Points. A $500 eligible American Airlines purchase earns 1,500 miles and 500 Loyalty Points from the card, in addition to whatever the passenger earns for flying. The 6 miles per dollar on eligible AAdvantage Hotels bookings are separate from the miles and Loyalty Points awarded for the hotel reservation itself. (Reserve Now, Pay Later bookings don’t qualify for the card’s 6-mile earning rate.) For my own spending, Executive already offers 4 miles per dollar on eligible American purchases (and at 4 points per dollar, I actually prefer my Chase Sapphire Reserve® [See rates and fees]) and 12 on eligible AAdvantage Hotels bookings. Globe’s Splurge Credit can give me a reason to charge a particular hotel purchase to it, but the regular earning rate doesn’t. For everyday purchases, one American mile and one Loyalty Point per dollar can make sense when you’re trying to reach a status threshold. Otherwise, there are better returns available. Holding Globe doesn’t obligate you to make it your everyday spending card. It’s a good card to have, not a daily spend driver outside of the quest for status. Four Admirals Club Passes Each Calendar Year Globe comes with four digital Admirals Club passes each calendar year. Each is valid for 24 hours after activation, including visits to multiple Admirals Clubs during that period. The access rules make these especially useful for an occasional traveler with children: Each adult needs a pass. Each adult using a pass can bring up to three children under 18. The primary cardmember must be present, including when using passes for adult companions. You need a same-day eligible American Airlines or oneworld boarding pass. Unused passes expire at the end of the calendar year. A couple traveling with two young children would use two passes for a travel day, rather than four. But you can’t give the passes to relatives traveling without you, and these aren’t Flagship Lounge passes or a full membership with partner lounge privileges. In my experience, the usual capacity restrictions on purchased one-day passes don’t apply to Globe passes. And just because you see a sign saying day passes aren’t being accepted doesn’t mean they aren’t being accepted – sometimes they just don’t take away the sign. American sells ordinary day passes for $79. That doesn’t make four Globe passes worth $316 to everyone. I already have Admirals Club membership through Executive, so I don’t assign these passes additional value for my own access. The Companion Certificate Doesn’t Require Annual Spending After renewing the card, starting in your second cardmembership year, you receive a certificate for one companion to travel on an eligible domestic roundtrip for $99 plus taxes and fees when you buy a qualifying Main Cabin roundtrip. However, this isn’t a certificate for any flight you want. It has fare inventory restrictions and restricted dates. You book through American Airlines Meeting Services, and travel generally must be within the contiguous 48 states on American or American Eagle. Residents of Alaska, Hawaii, Puerto Rico and the U.S. Virgin Islands have exceptions allowing qualifying trips from home to the lower 48. It doesn’t cover basic economy or partner flights. The primary cardmember must travel. The account must remain open for a full billing cycle after the anniversary month, and Citi allows 8–10 weeks for the certificate to become available. The certificate is valid for 12 months from issuance, with booking and travel completed by its expiration. I’ve gotten good savings from Barclays companion certificates, so I don’t dismiss these. If the eligible companion ticket would otherwise cost $500, replacing that with $99 plus taxes can cover much of the annual fee. The Credits Are Worth What They Save You Citi advertises more than $750 in value. I wouldn’t start with that number, but several benefits overlap with what I already have, and others require purchases I wouldn’t otherwise make. Up to $100 annual Splurge Credit. Choose up to two eligible merchants at a time from AAdvantage Hotels, 1stDibs, Future Personal Training and Live Nation. Activate your selection at Citi’s Splurge Credit page before purchasing. This is $100 total (not $100 per merchant). Eligible AAdvantage Hotels bookings are likely the most practical use for many readers. Up to $100 in annual inflight credits. Use the card for eligible purchases on domestic American Airlines or American Eagle flights. Food, drinks and eligible Wi-Fi purchases can qualify. This is less valuable when drinks are already included in your seat or status benefits, or when your flight has free Wi-Fi. Up to $240 annually with Turo. This is up to $30 per completed trip, so it takes eight trips to get the full amount. Link the card at Turo’s Globe page and pay with it directly; digital wallet payments don’t qualify. I wouldn’t assign this much value unless I were already using Turo regularly. Up to $120 for Global Entry or TSA PreCheck every four years. Useful if you need it, but I have plenty of other cards offering this reimbursement. My original reaction to the Splurge Credit was that it wasn’t worth much to me. I already have plenty of hotel credits. And an AAdvantage Hotels booking generally means giving up the hotel points, elite night credit and status benefits you’d receive by booking directly with a chain. I like the inflight credit myself now that American offers more food for purchase on more flights – I get one item free as an Executive Platinum member but I can buy sandwiches and snacks for my family. The calendar-year benefits also improve the first year. Open a card in November, and you can use available credits and passes before year-end and receive fresh allotments in January, before the next annual fee. Flight Streak resets in March. The companion certificate starts after renewal. Bags, Boarding And Other Benefits Of The Citi AAdvantage Globe Card The card provides a first checked bag free on qualifying domestic American Airlines itineraries for the primary cardmember and up to eight companions on the same reservation. Group 5 boarding also covers up to eight companions. You don’t have to pay for the tickets with Globe. Those can be valuable for someone without status, particularly a family traveling together. They add little for me because my existing status already provides better benefits. Your AAdvantage miles also don’t expire while you’re the primary holder of an eligible AAdvantage credit card. There’s also a 10% discount on eligible non-flight components of American Airlines Vacations packages booked through the designated Citi booking page. The travel and purchase protections include trip cancellation and interruption, trip delay, lost or damaged luggage, rental car coverage, extended warranty and purchase protection. Rental coverage is secondary in your country of residence. Citi Entertainment and Mastercard’s World Legend benefits add access to selected ticketing, dining and other experiences. I’ll Pay $350 To Keep The Citi AAdvantage Globe Card If you only want a checked bag and earlier boarding, Citi® / AAdvantage® Platinum Select® World Elite Mastercard® [See rates and fees] is cheaper. If you want regular Admirals Club access, Executive provides a membership for its $695 annual fee. Globe earns its place with the combination of flight bonuses, occasional lounge access and a companion certificate without an annual spending requirement. There’s a case for holding Globe alongside Executive for the additional Loyalty Points. Here’s how I’d look at renewal. If you get a real $100 of savings from the Splurge Credit, there’s $250 of annual fee left to justify through the flight bonus, companion certificate and other benefits. Earning all 15,000 Flight Streak Loyalty Points at that cost works out to about 1.67 cents per point before assigning any value to the remaining benefits. An extra 15,000 that gets you to the next status level is much more useful than points that leave you between thresholds. For someone flying at least 12 qualifying segments and pursuing American status, I think Globe is a strong addition even with another AAdvantage card. The Citi AAdvantage Globe Card awards 5,000 Loyalty Points for every four qualifying American Airlines flight segments, up to three times per status qualification year.

These are segments, so a roundtrip with a connection each way is four flights. Three of those trips can generate the full bonus. Six nonstop roundtrips would do it, too.

You don’t have to buy the tickets with your Globe card. You can use another card for its rewards or protections, or fly on a ticket your employer purchases, and still earn the bonus on your qualifying travel.

I view the card as an inexpensive way to purchase Loyalty Points which are valuable both for earning status and for additional milestone rewards.

The access rules make these especially useful for an occasional traveler with children: Each adult needs a pass. Each adult using a pass can bring up to three children under 18. The primary cardmember must be present, including when using passes for adult companions. You need a same-day eligible American Airlines or oneworld boarding pass. Unused passes expire at the end of the calendar year. A couple traveling with two young children would use two passes for a travel day, rather than four. But you can’t give the passes to relatives traveling without you, and these aren’t Flagship Lounge passes or a full membership with partner lounge privileges. In my experience, the usual capacity restrictions on purchased one-day passes don’t apply to Globe passes. And just because you see a sign saying day passes aren’t being accepted doesn’t mean they aren’t being accepted – sometimes they just don’t take away the sign. American sells ordinary day passes for $79. That doesn’t make four Globe passes worth $316 to everyone. I already have Admirals Club membership through Executive, so I don’t assign these passes additional value for my own access. The Companion Certificate Doesn’t Require Annual Spending After renewing the card, starting in your second cardmembership year, you receive a certificate for one companion to travel on an eligible domestic roundtrip for $99 plus taxes and fees when you buy a qualifying Main Cabin roundtrip. However, this isn’t a certificate for any flight you want. It has fare inventory restrictions and restricted dates. You book through American Airlines Meeting Services, and travel generally must be within the contiguous 48 states on American or American Eagle. Residents of Alaska, Hawaii, Puerto Rico and the U.S. Virgin Islands have exceptions allowing qualifying trips from home to the lower 48. It doesn’t cover basic economy or partner flights. The primary cardmember must travel. The account must remain open for a full billing cycle after the anniversary month, and Citi allows 8–10 weeks for the certificate to become available. The certificate is valid for 12 months from issuance, with booking and travel completed by its expiration. I’ve gotten good savings from Barclays companion certificates, so I don’t dismiss these. If the eligible companion ticket would otherwise cost $500, replacing that with $99 plus taxes can cover much of the annual fee. The Credits Are Worth What They Save You Citi advertises more than $750 in value. I wouldn’t start with that number, but several benefits overlap with what I already have, and others require purchases I wouldn’t otherwise make. Up to $100 annual Splurge Credit. Choose up to two eligible merchants at a time from AAdvantage Hotels, 1stDibs, Future Personal Training and Live Nation. Activate your selection at Citi’s Splurge Credit page before purchasing. This is $100 total (not $100 per merchant). Eligible AAdvantage Hotels bookings are likely the most practical use for many readers. Up to $100 in annual inflight credits. Use the card for eligible purchases on domestic American Airlines or American Eagle flights. Food, drinks and eligible Wi-Fi purchases can qualify. This is less valuable when drinks are already included in your seat or status benefits, or when your flight has free Wi-Fi. Up to $240 annually with Turo. This is up to $30 per completed trip, so it takes eight trips to get the full amount. Link the card at Turo’s Globe page and pay with it directly; digital wallet payments don’t qualify. I wouldn’t assign this much value unless I were already using Turo regularly. Up to $120 for Global Entry or TSA PreCheck every four years. Useful if you need it, but I have plenty of other cards offering this reimbursement. My original reaction to the Splurge Credit was that it wasn’t worth much to me. I already have plenty of hotel credits. And an AAdvantage Hotels booking generally means giving up the hotel points, elite night credit and status benefits you’d receive by booking directly with a chain. I like the inflight credit myself now that American offers more food for purchase on more flights – I get one item free as an Executive Platinum member but I can buy sandwiches and snacks for my family. The calendar-year benefits also improve the first year. Open a card in November, and you can use available credits and passes before year-end and receive fresh allotments in January, before the next annual fee. Flight Streak resets in March. The companion certificate starts after renewal. Bags, Boarding And Other Benefits Of The Citi AAdvantage Globe Card The card provides a first checked bag free on qualifying domestic American Airlines itineraries for the primary cardmember and up to eight companions on the same reservation. Group 5 boarding also covers up to eight companions. You don’t have to pay for the tickets with Globe. Those can be valuable for someone without status, particularly a family traveling together. They add little for me because my existing status already provides better benefits. Your AAdvantage miles also don’t expire while you’re the primary holder of an eligible AAdvantage credit card. There’s also a 10% discount on eligible non-flight components of American Airlines Vacations packages booked through the designated Citi booking page. The travel and purchase protections include trip cancellation and interruption, trip delay, lost or damaged luggage, rental car coverage, extended warranty and purchase protection. Rental coverage is secondary in your country of residence. Citi Entertainment and Mastercard’s World Legend benefits add access to selected ticketing, dining and other experiences. I’ll Pay $350 To Keep The Citi AAdvantage Globe Card If you only want a checked bag and earlier boarding, Citi® / AAdvantage® Platinum Select® World Elite Mastercard® [See rates and fees] is cheaper. If you want regular Admirals Club access, Executive provides a membership for its $695 annual fee. Globe earns its place with the combination of flight bonuses, occasional lounge access and a companion certificate without an annual spending requirement. There’s a case for holding Globe alongside Executive for the additional Loyalty Points. Here’s how I’d look at renewal. If you get a real $100 of savings from the Splurge Credit, there’s $250 of annual fee left to justify through the flight bonus, companion certificate and other benefits. Earning all 15,000 Flight Streak Loyalty Points at that cost works out to about 1.67 cents per point before assigning any value to the remaining benefits. An extra 15,000 that gets you to the next status level is much more useful than points that leave you between thresholds. For someone flying at least 12 qualifying segments and pursuing American status, I think Globe is a strong addition even with another AAdvantage card. Bonus categories increase redeemable miles, not Loyalty Points. A $500 eligible American Airlines purchase earns 1,500 miles and 500 Loyalty Points from the card, in addition to whatever the passenger earns for flying.

The 6 miles per dollar on eligible AAdvantage Hotels bookings are separate from the miles and Loyalty Points awarded for the hotel reservation itself. (Reserve Now, Pay Later bookings don’t qualify for the card’s 6-mile earning rate.)

For my own spending, Executive already offers 4 miles per dollar on eligible American purchases (and at 4 points per dollar, I actually prefer my Chase Sapphire Reserve® [See rates and fees]) and 12 on eligible AAdvantage Hotels bookings. Globe’s Splurge Credit can give me a reason to charge a particular hotel purchase to it, but the regular earning rate doesn’t.

For everyday purchases, one American mile and one Loyalty Point per dollar can make sense when you’re trying to reach a status threshold. Otherwise, there are better returns available. Holding Globe doesn’t obligate you to make it your everyday spending card. It’s a good card to have, not a daily spend driver outside of the quest for status.

An extra 15,000 that gets you to the next status level is much more useful than points that leave you between thresholds.

For someone flying at least 12 qualifying segments and pursuing American status, I think Globe is a strong addition even with another AAdvantage card.

#6064. Hyatt Keeps Pepsi For 10 More Years At 700+ U.S. Hotels—Even Though Few Guests Want It

Hyatt has signed up for another 10 years with Pepsi, covering more than 700 U.S. hotels. After Marriott finally decided to switch to Coca-Cola, Hyatt is sticking with the beverage that prompts a question nobody wants to hear: Is Pepsi okay? No, it isn’t. I rarely drink soda. When I do, I don’t want to waste it on Pepsi. The renewal announced November 19, flagged by The Bulkhead Seat, doesn’t cover every Hyatt brand or every country. But the economics of choosing Pepsi make more sense once you realize that the person negotiating the contract isn’t the one that has to drink it. Which Hyatt Brands Are Covered, And Where Can You Get Coke? The agreement covers U.S. hotels in Hyatt’s Classics and Essentials portfolios. Translating Hyatt’s brand groupings: Portfolio Brands Classics Grand Hyatt, Hyatt Regency, Destination by Hyatt, Hyatt Centric, Hyatt Vacation Club, Hyatt Essentials Hyatt Place, Hyatt House, Hyatt Studios, Hyatt Select, Caption by Hyatt, Unscripted by Hyatt UrCove also belongs to Essentials, but its Chinese hotels aren’t covered by a U.S. agreement. The Luxury, Lifestyle and Inclusive Collection portfolios aren’t part of this deal. No one wants to show up at an Andaz or Park Hyatt and get told they can’t have a Coke. Alila, Thompson, The Standard, and Hyatt Ziva and Zilara are also outside the deal’s scope. Here are some hotels that have specifically listed Coke: Hotel Coca-Cola On The Menu Park Hyatt New York Room service lists Coke and Diet Coke Andaz Maui Meeting and event menus list Coke and Diet Coke Thompson Dallas Room service lists Coke and Diet Coke Alila Marea Beach Resort Encinitas Room service lists bottled Coke Pepsi Doesn’t Have To Be Your First Choice To Win The Business When I covered Marriott’s switch in April, Marriott told hotels that more than 70% of its guests favored the Coca-Cola portfolio. Hotels choose suppliers based on the total deal: product pricing, rebates, equipment, servicing, marketing support and sometimes direct payments. We can see how this works in a public contract. Fresno, California’s 2018 Pepsi agreement for its convention center offered a $20,000 annual sponsorship payment, a 25% vending commission, $3 rebates per case or gallon sold, bulk pricing and equipment maintenance in exchange for exclusive beverage rights. A hotel has a modestly captive audience. You’ve already booked the room, your conference is downstairs, or you’re sitting by the pool. You can buy a Coke elsewhere, but that takes effort. Some people accept Pepsi. Others choose something else. The hotel loses some beverage sales and creates some disappointment. But it still thinks it can come out ahead if its supplier prices and rebates are better and they aren’t seeing guests change their hotel bookings. In other words, the worse product can be more profitable to the hotel – or at least to Hyatt corporate. Here, Hyatt brings access to guests whose hotel decision usually turns on something other than soda. Pepsi doesn’t have to persuade all those guests that it tastes better (it doesn’t). Getting its products stocked on property can shift purchases without changing anyone’s preferences. PepsiCo also brings Gatorade, Starbucks ready-to-drink coffee, Quaker, Lay’s, Doritos, Muscle Milk and poppi. “Is Pepsi Okay?” Was Never A Compliment The question assumes you’ve requested something else and asks whether you’ll accept a substitute you didn’t want. Pepsi understood the problem well enough to build its 2019 Super Bowl commercial around it, recruiting Steve Carell, Cardi B and Lil Jon to insist Pepsi was “More Than OK.” John Belushi’s Olympia Restaurant on Saturday Night Live had already reduced the experience to “No Coke! Pepsi!” You could order what you wanted. You were getting what the restaurant had decided to sell. The Pepsi Challenge, New Coke, And What A Recipe Can’t Copy I remember the Pepsi Challenge as a kid. I remember how scared Coke seemed, and the debacle of New Coke. The explanation popularized by Malcolm Gladwell in Blink is that Pepsi’s sweetness does better in a sip test than when someone drinks a whole can. Maybe some people really did prefer the first sip of Pepsi and then found the rest too much. That never seemed right to me. The first sip of Coke is much better. Fortunately, there’s no rule you have to finish a soda. Coca-Cola’s history of New Coke says the company’s lead over its chief competitor had been slipping for 15 consecutive years. It introduced the reformulated drink on April 23, 1985, after taste tests involving nearly 200,000 consumers favored the new formula. The original came back just 79 days later. The tests hadn’t captured how people would react to having their Coke taken away. The company could produce a drink that performed better in a test and still make customers furious by replacing the one they loved. That helps explain why Coke’s business is so hard to recreate even if someone could duplicate the liquid. The secret formula gets the attention, but a competitor would also need to reproduce decades of habits, memories, advertising and confidence that the drink will be what you expect. A familiar brand changes the experience of drinking it. Then there’s the distribution system: bottlers, delivery routes, coolers, fountains and relationships with stores and restaurants. Being easy to find reinforces the habit of asking for Coke. You know there’s already a strong likelihood it’ll be there when you ask. I don’t ask for my preferred drinks outside of places I know it’s available. Would you ask for Golden Elephant Three Lotus Pure Palm Juice at a diner off the New Jersey Turnpike? I don’t drink enough soda to make defending Coke a daily activity. If I’m going to have soda, Dr. Brown’s cream is my first choice, followed by their black cherry. Hyatt can negotiate all the Pepsi it wants. I’ll just have water, thanks.
